Definition: from G2660; a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with G3506 or even with G3571)) stupor (lethargy):--slumber.
BiblicalUsage: God gave them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see and ears that they should not hear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a slumbering spirit is the saddest judgment of all, because the truth is preached and the ears are closed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
